CVE-2026-20127.description:
A vulnerability in the peering authentication in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Validator, formerly SD-WAN vBond, could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system.

This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.

CVE-2026-109411.description: An access control bypass flaw was found in Samba's vfs_ceph_rgw module in it's openat() function. An authenticated user can bypass access controls to read or overwrite restricted files on shares configured with the experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module. When a client requests an existing file using mismatched character casing, the module fails to perform a case-insensitive lookup correctly, causing the server to treat the operation as creating a new file. As a result, the server skips standard permission checks on the existing file, allowing the attacker to access or overwrite sensitive data owned by other users.

CVE-2026-118659.description: Happy DOM is a JavaScript implementation of a web browser without its graphical user interface. Prior to 21.0.2, the Happy DOM server-renderer package's ServerRendererServer accepts unauthenticated HTTP/2 requests and resolves attacker-controlled :path values against server.targetOrigin in #onIncomingRequest in packages/@happy-dom/server-renderer/src/ServerRendererServer.ts without confirming that the resolved origin remains trusted before calling fetch. A protocol-relative path can change the destination to an arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS endpoint reachable by the server, including local and internal services, and the proxy relays the fetched response headers and body to the requester. This issue is fixed in version 21.0.2.

CVE-2026-118660.description: Happy DOM is a JavaScript implementation of a web browser without its graphical user interface. Prior to 21.0.0, Happy DOM loads iframe src URLs and link rel="stylesheet" href URLs by default while parsing untrusted HTML on the server because disableIframePageLoading and disableCSSFileLoading default to false. An attacker who controls parsed HTML can therefore cause server-side requests to arbitrary internal or cloud endpoints without an application opt-in and may expose confidential responses or credentials returned by those endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 21.0.0.

posts.content:
Endor Labs’ AI SAST found two Apache Kafka zero-days, now fixed: CVE-2026-114349 and CVE-2026-111551. Payloads: 90, 9, and 12 bytes. Upgrade to 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0 and set max.decompressed.message.bytes
https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/endor-labs-ai-sast-finds-two-apache-kafka-zero-days-unbounded-memory-allocation-from-brokers-to-kafka-streams?

CVE-2026-114349.description:
When a broker decodes a compressed record batch, the per-record decoder reads a declared body size from the decompressed stream and allocates a buffer of that size before validating it against the bytes available or any configured limit. The size is attacker-controlled, and the batch CRC does not constrain it, so a small (around 90-byte), CRC-valid compressed produce request can declare a body size of up to about 2 GiB and force the broker to attempt that allocation, raising OutOfMemoryError. The record size limit (max.message.bytes), the request size limit, and client/broker quotas bound only the compressed wire size, not the declared decompressed size.


Impact:

An authenticated principal with Write on a topic can crash broker request-handler threads (reached when a batch's codec differs from the topic's compression.type and records are re-encoded) and any consumer that fetches the record, denying service. On brokers started with -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError, a common hardening, a single crafted request terminates the broker JVM. More seriously, a crafted record  is accepted at ingest and written to disk; when the log-cleaner later reads it on a compacted topic, the OutOfMemoryError (an Error, not an Exception) terminates the cleaner thread, which is not restarted. With the default of a single cleaner thread, log compaction then stops for the entire broker, including the internal __consumer_offsets and __transaction_state topics, and the condition persists across restarts until the offending record is removed. The impact is availability only; no data is disclosed or altered.


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0, and set max.decompressed.message.bytes (at the broker and/or topic level) to a bounded value appropriate for your workload. Upgrading alone is not sufficient: for backward compatibility this configuration defaults to an effectively unlimited value (about 2 GiB), so a broker remains exposed until the limit is set. Choose a value at or slightly above the largest legitimate decompressed record your applications produce, and comfortably below the broker heap divided by the number of request-handler and cleaner threads. Until you can upgrade and configure the limit, restrict Write access to trusted producers; quotas and max.message.bytes do not mitigate this issue.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: the broker validates a record's declared decompressed body size against max.decompressed.message.bytes before allocating, on the produce-validation, log-compaction, and timestamp-lookup paths, and rejects oversized or negative sizes with InvalidRecordException. Operators must set this configuration to a bounded value to be protected, as its default is effectively unlimited.

posts.content:
Endor Labs’ AI SAST found two Apache Kafka zero-days, now fixed: CVE-2026-114349 and CVE-2026-111551. Payloads: 90, 9, and 12 bytes. Upgrade to 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0 and set max.decompressed.message.bytes
https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/endor-labs-ai-sast-finds-two-apache-kafka-zero-days-unbounded-memory-allocation-from-brokers-to-kafka-streams?

CVE-2026-111551.description:
Several Kafka deserialization paths read a size or count field from input data and use it directly to allocate an array, collection, or byte buffer, with no check against the bytes actually available. A small crafted input can therefore declare a very large size and force a multi-gigabyte allocation. The affected paths are, in Kafka Streams, ProcessorRecordContext (header count), ChangedDeserializer (varint value length), CombinedKeySchema (foreign-key length, which could also produce a negative size), ProcessorMetadata (key length), and AssignmentInfo group-assignment decoding; and, in the clients library, ListDeserializer (used by ListSerde).


Impact:

An attacker can trigger the oversized allocation and raise an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the affected consumer or Kafka Streams thread; the broker and the rest of the cluster are unaffected. The reachable surface depends on the path: writing a crafted record to a Streams application's internal changelog or repartition topics, or committing crafted offset metadata to its consumer group (Streams internal paths); writing a crafted record to any topic that a consumer reads with ListSerde (ListDeserializer); or, as a member of a Streams consumer group, returning crafted assignment data when elected leader (AssignmentInfo). Because a crafted record remains in its topic, the error can recur on restart. The record size limit (max.message.bytes) does not help, because the allocation is driven by a size field rather than by the input's length.


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. Where authorization is enabled, restrict write access to each application's internal topics and consumer group to its own principal, and restrict who can produce to topics that are consumed with ListSerde.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: these deserialization paths validate the declared size against the remaining input before allocating and reject input that fails the check.

zip is a zip library for Rust that supports reading and writing simple ZIP files. Through 9.0.4, ZipArchive treats Central Directory File Header filenames as authoritative while ZipStreamReader extracts using Local File Header filenames without reconciling the duplicate metadata in src/read/stream.rs. A crafted archive can therefore appear benign to a component that inspects the central directory but cause a streaming extractor to write a different attacker-selected path and content, potentially overwriting files used by a downstream service. This issue is fixed in version 9.0.5.

CVE ID: CVE-2026-46300
Vendor: Linux
Product: Kernel
Date Added: 2026-10-28
CVE URL: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46300

CVE-2026-46300.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

Defused recorded exploratory exploitation attempts against its Oracle EBS decoys on October 27, one week after Oracle released patches. Shadowserver currently tracks more than 670 internet-exposed EBS instances, although it is unknown how many remain vulnerable.

CVE-2026-118650.description:
## Summary

When `middleware.Static` is mounted globally (`e.Use(middleware.Static(...))`) and an application relies on a **route- or group-level middleware guard** to restrict a path that also falls under the served static root, a `%2F`-encoded request bypasses that guard while the file is still served. This is the same encoding/decoding mismatch fixed for `StaticFS`/`StaticDirectoryHandler` in CVE-2026-55677 / GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq, but the fix did not cover the `middleware.Static` path. In addition, the `StaticConfig.EnablePathUnescaping` docstring states the default configuration prevents exactly this bypass, which is inaccurate for the global-mount case.

**This is not path traversal:** no file outside the static root is accessed. The served file lives inside the static root; the issue is that access-control expectations set by a route guard are inconsistent between the literal and `%2F`-encoded forms of the same path.

## Details

Root cause — the router and the static handler disagree on how to interpret `%2F`:

- The router matches routes on the **raw, still-encoded** path, so `GET /admin%2Fsecret.txt` does **not** match a `/admin/...` route or group; any middleware attached to that route/group is therefore skipped.
- `middleware.Static` selects its path source in `middleware/static.go` (~L219): with a global `e.Use` mount there is no wildcard route, so it uses `c.Request().URL.Path`, which `net/http` has already **decoded** (`%2F` → `/`). It then `path.Clean`s (~L235) and `Open`s (~L259) `admin/secret.txt`, serving the file.

Net effect: for the literal path the guard runs; for the `%2F`-encoded path the guard is skipped but the same file is served.

Relevant code:
- `middleware/static.go` ~L219 (`p := c.Request().URL.Path`), ~L235 (`path.Clean`), ~L259 (`currentFS.Open`)
- `StaticConfig.EnablePathUnescaping` docstring (`static.go` ~L60-67) — claims the default prevents the `/admin%2fprivate.txt` → `/admin/*` guard bypass; this is not true for the global mount.

Relationship to prior advisories:
- **CVE-2026-55677 / GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq** (patched 5.2.0): same `%2F` router-vs-handler mismatch, but fixed for `StaticFS`/`StaticDirectoryHandler`. The `middleware.Static` path was not covered — this report is that gap.
- **CVE-2026-25766 / GHSA-pgvm-wxw2-hrv9** (patched 5.0.3): a *different* issue (Windows backslash traversal **outside** the root). Referenced only to disambiguate; not the same as this report.

## PoC

Environment: `golang:1.25`, module using the official release (`go get github.com/labstack/echo/v5@v5.3.1`, no local `replace`). Static root `public/` contains a marker file `public/admin/secret.txt` = `SECRET`.

Minimal app (the pattern under test: static served globally + a group guard intended to protect `/admin`):

```go
package main

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
	"github.com/labstack/echo/v5/middleware"
)

func main() {
	e := echo.New()
	e.Use(middleware.Static("public")) // serves ./public globally (default filesystem)

	admin := e.Group("/admin", func(next echo.HandlerFunc) echo.HandlerFunc {
		return func(c *echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusUnauthorized, "auth required") }
	})
	admin.GET("/secret.txt", func(c *echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "handler") })

	e.Start(":1323")
}
```

Requests (unauthenticated):

```
# Literal: route matches -> group guard runs
curl -i http://localhost:1323/admin/secret.txt
# => 401

# %2F-encoded: route does NOT match -> guard skipped, but middleware.Static serves the file
curl -i --path-as-is http://localhost:1323/admin%2Fsecret.txt
# => 200, body: SECRET
```

Observed on `v5.3.1`: literal → `401`; `%2F` → `200` with the file contents. For contrast, serving via the (patched) `e.StaticFS("/")` returns `404` for the same `%2F` request, showing the `middleware.Static` path was not covered by the CVE-2026-55677 fix.

## Impact

An unauthenticated remote user can retrieve a file served by `middleware.Static` even when the application attached a route/group middleware guard to that path, by substituting `/` with `%2F`. The consequence is limited to files already inside the served static root (CWE-863 authorization inconsistency; CWE-436 interpretation conflict) — **there is no access to files outside the static root**.

**Honest caveat on validity / severity:** this only has security impact for applications that (a) serve a directory statically to the public *and* (b) place a sensitive file inside that same directory while relying on a *route-level* guard to protect it. That combination is arguably a misconfiguration — a statically-served directory is public by design — so maintainers may reasonably classify this as a documentation fix (correct the `EnablePathUnescaping` claim) or won't-fix rather than a code vulnerability. It is filed primarily because (1) the router-vs-handler `%2F` inconsistency is the exact class fixed in CVE-2026-55677 but left uncovered for `middleware.Static`, and (2) the docstring currently promises protection it does not provide.

## Patches

Fixed in `github.com/labstack/echo/v5` v5.4.0 and `github.com/labstack/echo/v4` v4.16.0. With the default settings, the Static middleware resolves files from the same form of the path that the router matched, so percent-encoded paths such as `/admin%2Fsecret.txt` or `/%61dmin/secret.txt` no longer reach a file under a guarded route. Paths with `.`, `..` or empty segments are no longer served.

Note: middleware registered with `Echo#Use` runs before route and group middleware, so route guards never protect files served by a global Static middleware. Keep protected files outside its root directory, or serve them with `Echo#Static` behind the guard.

## Workarounds

Keep files that need protection outside the Static middleware's root directory.

CVE-2026-61542.description: Gearboy is a Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Super Game Boy emulator and debugger with an embedded MCP server. Gearsystem, the affected component, has an optional `--mcp-http` mode that accepts unauthenticated MCP requests from any reachable network peer despite localhost-only documentation and logging. In the described `platforms/shared/desktop/mcp/mcp_transport.h` transport, the socket binds `INADDR_ANY`, normally on port 7777, and POST requests to `/mcp` reach dispatch without `Authorization`, `Host`, or `Origin` checks. Responses and OPTIONS advertise `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. A peer can initialize an MCP session and invoke exposed emulator/debugging operations; even a garbage bearer token does not block dispatch, while a loopback-bind negative control prevents network access. The reported impact is bounded to the emulator process, debugging state, and local files accepted as media, rather than demonstrated host code execution. Gearboy 3.8.7 contains a patch.

CISA has added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation.

Known collectively as PHP2Shell, the two memory corruption flaws can allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code on PHP systems serving web requests.

• PHP 8.5.12

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 CISA confirms critical PHP2Shell flaws are now being exploited in attacks

CISA has added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation.
⠀
Known collectively as PHP2Shell, the two memory corruption flaws can allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code on PHP systems serving web requests.

Affected configurations include PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The PHP team considers mod_php installations at the highest risk.
⠀
Both vulnerabilities have a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2.

Fixed versions:

• PHP 8.5.12
• PHP 8.4.27
• PHP 8.3.36
• PHP 8.2.35
⠀
CISA has ordered U.S. federal agencies to remediate the vulnerabilities by October 29.

The PHP team says there are no complete mitigations and that updating is the only safe solution.

Source: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 Critical 16-year-old EDK II flaw enables code execution before Secure Boot

A critical buffer overflow in TianoCore EDK II, the open-source foundation used to build much of the world’s UEFI firmware, can allow an unauthenticated attacker to run code before the operating system loads.

Tracked as CVE-2026-97631, the vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.5 and has existed in the code since November 2010.
⠀
The flaw resides in the PXE network-boot driver, which copies incoming ICMP error messages into a fixed 504-byte buffer without properly limiting their size.
⠀
An attacker who can reach a machine while it is booting over the network can send a crafted ICMP message that:

• Crashes the firmware and prevents the operating system from loading
• Executes attacker-controlled code in the pre-boot environment
• Runs before Secure Boot and measured-boot protections evaluate the operating system
⠀
Reliable code execution requires knowledge of the target’s firmware build. Systems that boot exclusively from local storage are not exposed through this attack path.
⠀
An upstream fix was merged into EDK II on October 15, but no stable EDK II release currently includes it. Server and motherboard vendors must integrate the patch and distribute BIOS or UEFI updates to customers.

Source: https://github.com/tianocore/edk2/security/advisories/GHSA-99cj-7hg9-mp4m

🚨🇦🇪 Telegram zero-day can enable code execution through malicious animated content

A vulnerability in Telegram’s rlottie animation library can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code within the application process.

Tracked as CVE-2026-111105, the flaw carries a CVSS score of 7.0 and was publicly disclosed by Trend Micro’s Zero Day Initiative after remaining unresolved at the client-code level.
⠀
The vulnerability is caused by improper validation of attacker-controlled animation data, resulting in a write before the beginning of an allocated memory buffer.
⠀
Despite reports describing the flaw as a zero-click sticker attack, ZDI’s final advisory says user interaction is required. The victim must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file for exploitation to occur.
⠀
Telegram told ZDI that server-side sticker validation mitigates the vulnerability. However, ZDI continued seeking a client-side fix and ultimately published the issue as a zero-day advisory on October 15.
⠀
No affected client versions, patched versions or confirmed in-the-wild attacks have been disclosed.

Users should keep Telegram updated and avoid opening untrusted animated files, sticker packs or external links until a client-side fix is confirmed.

Source: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-757/

CVE-2026-111105.description:
Telegram rlottie Numeric Truncation Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Telegram. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the rlottie library. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write before the start of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30207.

posts.content:
🟠 CVE-2026-56828 - High (8.8)

Shopper is a Headless e-commerce Admin Panel. From 2.8.0 until 2.8.1, three Shopper Livewire admin components retain authorization gaps after the earlier team-settings authorization fix. A staff member with only `view_users` and `access_dashboard`...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-56828/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-56828.description:
## Summary

Three Livewire admin components in `shopper/framework` (latest master at commit `fcd0c59`, released as v2.8.0) gate state-mutating actions on the read-only `view_users` permission. This is the same class as the issue Shopper fixed in v2.8.0 / PR #511 / [GHSA-f946-9qp6-vgch](https://github.com/shopperlabs/shopper/security/advisories/GHSA-f946-9qp6-vgch) — the PR moved most write actions from `view_users` to `access_setting`, but three were missed (one of them is a brand-new file added by the security commit itself).

A staff user holding only `view_users` + `access_dashboard` (a realistic "support" or "viewer" role per Shopper's own `PermissionsTableSeeder`) can: (1) self-escalate by granting any permission to their own role; (2) create a brand-new admin team member with a chosen password and the `admin` role and then log in as that user; (3) delete arbitrary `permissions` rows (RBAC DoS) or — when `can_be_removed=true` — delete entire roles.

CVSS 3.1: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` = 8.8 (High). CWE-285 (Improper Authorization) + CWE-862 (Missing Authorization).

## Vulnerable components (paths relative to repo root)

### 1) `packages/admin/src/Livewire/Components/Settings/Team/Permissions.php`

- `togglePermission(int $id)` at line 28 calls `$this->authorize('view_users');`
- `removePermission(int $id)` at line 55 calls `$this->authorize('view_users');`

The Permissions blade at `packages/admin/resources/views/livewire/components/settings/team/permissions.blade.php` line 34 emits every permission's `id` directly in `wire:click` handlers, so the attacker does not even need to guess IDs — the page itself enumerates them.

Net effect: any user who can mount the Permissions component (gated on `view_users`) can grant any permission row to the bound `$role`. Granting `access_setting` to the attacker's own role unlocks every action that PR #511 supposedly hardened with `->authorize('access_setting')`. Granting `delete_customers`, `edit_orders`, `edit_products`, `add_brands`, etc. is direct data-modification escalation.

### 2) `packages/admin/src/Livewire/SlideOvers/CreateTeamMember.php`

- `mount()` at line 53 calls `$this->authorize('view_users');`
- `store()` at line 122 calls `$this->authorize('view_users');`

This file is `new file mode 100755` in commit `fcd0c59` — it was created as part of the security fix and inherited the same misclassified gate.

`store()` creates a `User` with `email_verified_at = now()`, the attacker's chosen password, and any selected `role_id`. The `Radio::make('role_id')` options filter only excludes `config('shopper.admin.roles.user')`, so the `admin` role is selectable. Log out, log in as the new account → full admin.

### 3) `packages/admin/src/Livewire/Pages/Settings/Team/RolePermission.php`

- `deleteAction` at lines 81-90: only gated by `->visible($this->role->can_be_removed)`, with no `->authorize()` chain.

Page-level `mount` (line 52) requires only `view_users`. For any role with `can_be_removed = true`, a `view_users`-only user can call the action and delete the role (cascading the loss of permissions for every assigned user).

## Self-confirmation in the project's own test suite

The following tests are green on master @ `fcd0c59` — they ARE the PoC:

```
tests/Admin/Livewire/Components/Settings/Team/PermissionsTest.php
  line 14-16: `givePermissionTo('view_users')` only
  line 36-45: "can toggle permission to role" — passes
  line 74-85: "can remove permission" — passes

tests/Admin/Livewire/SlideOvers/CreateTeamMemberTest.php
  line 16-18: `givePermissionTo('view_users')` only
  line 29-56: "can create new team member" — passes, asserts the new user `hasRole('manager')`
```

A `view_users`-only Livewire user actor successfully toggles permissions, removes permissions, and creates a new privileged user — verified by Shopper's own regression tests.

## Suggested fix

Change `$this->authorize('view_users')` to `$this->authorize('access_setting')` in:

- `Permissions::togglePermission`
- `Permissions::removePermission`
- `Permissions::mount` (defence in depth, matches `Team\Index`)
- `CreateTeamMember::mount`
- `CreateTeamMember::store`

Add `->authorize('access_setting')` to `RolePermission::deleteAction` (matches the pattern already applied to `generatePermissionsAction`, `createPermissionAction`, and `Team\Index::DeleteAction`).

Update the two regression tests to use `access_setting` instead of `view_users` so they accurately reflect the privilege boundary.

## Resources

- Prior advisory of the same class: https://github.com/shopperlabs/shopper/security/advisories/GHSA-f946-9qp6-vgch
- Fix commit that introduced these residual gaps: https://github.com/shopperlabs/shopper/commit/fcd0c5920588702df5b874f432b1042abd77a50b
- CWE-285 Improper Authorization
- CWE-862 Missing Authorization

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 Critical GoAhead flaw allows revoked certificates to bypass authentication

A critical vulnerability in the GoAhead embedded web server causes revoked client certificates to remain valid on certain mutual TLS deployments.

Tracked as CVE-2026-115881, the flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.1 and affects GoAhead versions 3.4.5 through 6.1.0.
⠀
GoAhead loads the configured certificate revocation list but fails to enable the OpenSSL flag that actually enforces it. An attacker possessing a previously trusted certificate and its private key could continue accessing protected services after the certificate was revoked.
⠀
Researchers also disclosed two related TLS flaws:

• CVE-2026-115884: Certain LibreSSL builds may accept an overlong certificate chain, CVSS 7.4
• GOAHEAD-SA-2026-0005: Mbed TLS builds may use a one-byte Diffie-Hellman modulus, allowing some recorded TLS 1.2 sessions to be decrypted, CVSS 5.9
⠀
GoAhead is embedded in management interfaces for routers, printers, gateways and industrial equipment.

Exposure depends on the TLS library and configuration used by each device, so the widespread use of GoAhead does not mean every device is vulnerable.
⠀
All three flaws were fixed in GoAhead 6.1.1. Device owners may need to wait for firmware containing the update from their equipment manufacturer.

Source: https://github.com/embedthis/goahead/security/advisories/GHSA-5m75-xq69-c3c5

Hey gang, the #infosec datascape is on fire again. And do *you* have any #IoT devices?

Critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in the #GoAhead embedded web server, affecting devices from major manufacturers like Palo Alto Networks, #Siemens, and #Boeing. The vulnerability impacts hundreds of millions of IoT, industrial control, and network devices, as many vendors have not yet issued firmware updates to address these specific flaws.

The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS 9.1), allows revoked client certificates to bypass security checks in OpenSSL, a critical risk for mutual-TLS (mTLS) configurations.

Also a weak key exchange in the Mbed TLS backend (CVSS 5.9) that can enable passive session decryption, and a certificate chain bypass in LibreSSL builds (CVSS 7.4).

Additionally, a login bypass vulnerability allows authentication with any password if the user's password is stored in the newer Blowfish format.

CVE-2026-116690.description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.10.0 until 3.17.0, the prompt branch in _create_model_version() accepts schemeless relative sources because path validation runs only when a source has a URL scheme, and mlflow.prompt.is_prompt is interpreted by tag presence rather than a true value. A remote caller can store a server-local path as the model version artifact location and use /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/get-artifact to read files accessible to the MLflow server process. MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py accepts request-selected descendants o...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-116692.description:
## Summary MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints: 1. Create an experiment whose local artifact location points to a writable allowed scorer package. 2. Create a run, causing MLflow to allocate `//artifacts/`. 3. Upload a Python module into that run artifact directory. 4. Submit a serialized third-party scorer whose module path resolves to the uploaded file. 5. Trigger server-side import and class construction through `/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke`. On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow v3.14.0 image, this produces unauthenticated arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the MLflow server process. The reproduced image runs the process as uid 0 and permits writes to its installed Python package tree. The attached proof of concept is intentionally harmless. The uploaded constructor performs one action only: it writes a random marker beside its own uploaded run artifact. The marker is then downloaded through MLflow's run-artifact endpoint and checked for an exact match. ## Technical details ### 1. The allow-list accepts attacker-created descendants At release commit `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c`, `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py` defines these allowed roots: ```python THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({ "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas", "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval", "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens", "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix", }) ``` In `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, the deserializer accepts either an exact root or any descendant: ```python module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".") ``` It then performs the following operations using request-controlled values: ```python module = importlib.import_module(module_path) scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None) scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs) ``` A package-name prefix is not a provenance boundary. If the server process can write below an allowed package, an attacker-created descendant can satisfy the string-prefix check and become importable Python code. Relevant source locations at the v3.14.0 release commit: * `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py`, allowed third-party scorer modules * `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, third-party scorer deserialization and construction ### 2. Deserialization occurs before trace processing In `mlflow/server/handlers.py`, `_invoke_scorer_handler()` parses the supplied serialized scorer and calls: ```python scorer = Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer) ``` Only after deserialization and construction does the handler call: ```python batches = get_trace_batches_for_scorer(trace_ids, scorer, tracking_store) ``` The attacker-controlled constructor therefore runs before the server validates or resolves the supplied trace IDs. The minimal proof class is deliberately not a complete MLflow scorer. After its constructor writes the marker, later trace-batching logic accesses scorer attributes that the proof class does not implement. The resulting HTTP 500 occurs after code execution and does not invalidate the proof. No background job execution or special job-execution server option is required to reach the constructor. ### 3. MLflow's artifact layout places the module under the trusted prefix The experiment creation endpoint accepts an `artifact_location`. For file-backed experiments, MLflow derives each run artifact directory as: ```text //artifacts/ ``` The proof of concept selects this package directory in the official v3.14.0 image: ```text file:///usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens ``` After creating a run and uploading `audit_.py`, the resulting filesystem location is: ```text /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens//artifacts/audit_.py ``` The corresponding import path is: ```text mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens..artifacts.audit_ ``` The attack does not overwrite an existing package module. It creates a new run-scoped module in the normal file-backed artifact layout. The run ID is returned to the caller. ### 4. Authentication and authorization behavior With authentication disabled, as in the default reproduced server configuration, no credentials are required. When MLflow basic authentication is enabled, authentication still applies. However, the scorer-invocation AJAX endpoint is assigned to `validate_gateway_proxy`, which returns `True` without performing an experiment- or scorer-level resource permission check. Practical exploitation in an authenticated deployment still requires the caller to create an experiment and run and upload artifacts to them. The key authorization issue is that scorer deserialization itself is not gated by a resource-specific permission check for the supplied experiment before the import occurs. ## Proof of concept The attached reproduction is intentionally isolated: * exact official MLflow v3.14.0 image pinned by manifest digest; * Docker network disabled; * MLflow bound to container loopback; * no shell command or external callback; * no external request; * no host filesystem write; * marker created beside the uploaded run artifact; * marker retrieved through the run-artifact download endpoint; and * disposable container removed after completion. Run: ```bash ./run-official-image.sh ``` Expected output: ```text MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 PACKAGE_DIR=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 INVOKE_STATUS=500 PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` The security-relevant result is: ```text PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` This proves that the attacker-controlled constructor executed in the MLflow server process before the later scorer-processing failure. ## Reproduction environment * **Release:** MLflow v3.14.0 * **Release commit:** `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c` * **Official image:** `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.14.0` * **Manifest digest:** `sha256:967de3ca34b6a5751718e380a0a383eb0ce1a6f5b484f363bd0da7559117a5f8` * **Python version:** 3.10.18 * **Image-configured user:** empty * **Observed runtime user:** uid 0 * **Server bind:** `127.0.0.1:5000` * **Container network:** disabled * **Backend store:** `sqlite:////work/mlflow.db` * **Default artifact root:** `/work/artifacts` * **Authentication:** disabled * **Special job-execution option:** none Server command inside the disposable container: ```bash mlflow server \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 5000 \ --backend-store-uri sqlite:////work/mlflow.db \ --default-artifact-root /work/artifacts ``` ## Affected range and source lineage The vulnerable third-party scorer deserialization behavior was introduced by commit: ```text 02eea26035b9d8e65af31e6e8f058ca195f62cdd Enable third-party scorer registration in OSS MLflow (#22634) ``` The feature is absent from v3.11.1 and first appears in v3.12.0. Runtime reproduction succeeds on v3.14.0. The relevant `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py` content is unchanged at master commit: ```text 20858c9426a9644dfcf9545a92cbb534376779eb ``` No fixed release was identified as of 2026-07-12. ## Impact On the reproduced stock no-auth image, any network caller who can reach the tracking server can execute Python code as the MLflow process without credentials or user interaction. Successful exploitation provides confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact over all data, credentials, network access, and filesystem locations available to the MLflow server process. The stock image's runtime uid 0 increases container-level impact. Host impact still depends on the container runtime configuration, mounted paths, granted capabilities, socket exposure, and other isolation controls. In authentication-enabled deployments, exploitation requires an authenticated principal capable of creating an experiment and run and uploading artifacts. The exact chain also requires the server process to be able to write beneath one of the allowed scorer packages. This condition holds in the reproduced official image and may hold in virtual environments installed and run by the same operating-system user. A read-only container filesystem or a scorer package directory owned by a different, non-writable user blocks this exact placement chain. ## Artifacts and attachments ### Remote proof-of-concept script POC Script: [new_remote_poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29936616/new_remote_poc.py) The remote proof of concept was then executed as follows. CVE-2026-59176.description: Functype is a family of TypeScript functional programming libraries. Prior to 1.4.4, the `set_functype_version` MCP tool in `functype-mcp-server` accepts an unconstrained `version` string using only `z.string()` validation in `packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts` and interpolates it into `functype@<version>` for `pnpm add`. Package-alias syntaxes such as `file:`, `npm:`, URLs, or paths can cause an arbitrary local or remote package to be installed as functype. Immediately afterward, `initDocsData(true)` in `packages/mcp-server/src/lib/docs/data.ts` resolves `functype/cli` and dynamically imports the newly installed module, executing attacker-controlled JavaScript with the MCP server process's privileges. Any MCP client able to send a `tools/call` request invoking the tool can exploit the flaw; the tool is enabled by default without authentication in `stdio` mode. A connected AI assistant susceptible to indirect prompt injection can also be induced to invoke it from a malicious document or web page. In non-default `TRANSPORT_TYPE=httpStream` deployments, a network-accessible attacker does not require local access. Successful execution can read process secrets, modify files, or terminate the server. This issue is fixed in `version` 1.4.4.

CVE-2026-59172.description: Joker is a small Clojure interpreter, linter and formatter written in Go. Prior to 1.8.2, `joker --lint <file>` walks upward from the linted file to locate a `.jokerd/` directory and executes matching `linter.*` files before linting. Those files contain executable Joker/Clojure code, so linting a file inside an untrusted repository can execute repository-supplied code with the linter user's privileges. Editor integrations and CI jobs that automatically lint checked-out source can trigger this behavior. The patch stops executing project-local linter customizations and loads executable customization only from the user's home directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.2.

🟠 CVE-2026-59185 - High (8.5)

identrail is a machine identity security platform for AWS, GitHub/OIDC, and Kubernetes. Prior to 1.0.2, the default-on `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/projects/:project_id/github/connect/complete` endpoint in `internal/api/router.go` accepts `i...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-59185/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-59185.description:
## Summary

identrail's GitHub App connection-completion endpoint binds a fully client-supplied `installation_id` to the caller's workspace without verifying that the installation belongs to, or was installed by, the workspace that initiated the connect flow. identrail then mints a GitHub App installation access token for the supplied `installation_id` using the app's own JWT, so an authenticated tenant can link any other identrail customer's GitHub App installation into their own workspace and read that victim organization's private repositories.

## Affected code (default-on path, no feature flag)

- Route: `internal/api/router.go:3590` — `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/projects/:project_id/github/connect/complete`. `installation_id` is read from the JSON body or the attacker-controlled `X-GitHub-Installation-ID` header (`router.go:3582-3588`).
- Service: `internal/api/github_connect.go:781` `CompleteGitHubConnection`. The `state` token IS rigorously bound to the caller's scope (`github_connect.go:818`: `if stateRecord.TenantID != scope.TenantID || stateRecord.WorkspaceID != project.WorkspaceID || stateRecord.ProjectID != project.ProjectID { ... }`), but the only check on `installation_id` is `request.InstallationID <= 0` (`:794`). The raw client value is persisted as the workspace's connection (`:840`).
- Cross-tenant read primitive: `internal/connectors/github/repositories.go:39` `ListInstallationRepositories` → `internal/connectors/github/app.go:170` mints a token via `POST /app/installations/{installationId}/access_tokens` signed with the App JWT, succeeding for any installation where identrail's app is installed.

The feature-flagged V2 path `CompleteGitHubConnector` (`github_connect.go:447`, default off) shares the gap and is additionally weaker (matches pending connector by `state` value alone with no caller-scope re-check); a single fix should cover both.

## Intent proof

The code binds `state` to `{TenantID, WorkspaceID, ProjectID}` and re-verifies it at completion (`:818`), demonstrating it understands binding is required. The asymmetry — `state` bound, `installation_id` unbound — is the missed check.

## Exploitation

1. Attacker is any authenticated identrail tenant; they call `StartGitHubConnection` for their own workspace and receive a `state`.
2. Attacker calls the completion route with `{state: <their state>, installation_id: V}` where V is a victim org's identrail GitHub App installation id (installation ids are not secret — they appear in post-install redirect URLs, webhook payloads, the org's GitHub App settings, and are enumerable integers).
3. `CompleteGitHubConnection` accepts (state matches attacker scope), `ListInstallationRepositories(V)` mints a token for V and lists the victim org's private repos, and the connection is persisted under the attacker's workspace.
4. Attacker now reads the victim org's private repository inventory and can drive posture scans/repo reads via their own workspace.

Impact: cross-tenant disclosure of another customer organization's private GitHub repositories and metadata.

## Remediation

Bind `installation_id` with the same rigor as `state`: capture it from GitHub's signed post-install redirect (`setup_url`/`callback_url`) and pin it to the pending state at start time, and/or after minting verify the installation's `account` matches the org the initiating workspace is authorized for.

CVE-2026-118485.description: Axel Download Accelerator 2.17.14 and earlier performs URL percent-decoding (http_decode()) on the output filename after the URL has been parsed and the filename component extracted. This allows an attacker to embed %2e%2e%2f (URL-encoded ../) sequences in the URL path. These sequences survive the URL parser intact (they contain no literal / characters) but are decoded into directory traversal sequences before the output file is opened for writing. As a result, a crafted URL can cause axel to write downloaded content to arbitrary filesystem paths relative to the current working directory.

Veeam has released security updates addressing five vulnerabilities across Backup & Replication, Veeam Agent for Linux and Veeam ONE.
⠀
The most serious, CVE-2026-108142, carries a CVSS score of 9.1 and allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authorization on the CDP Coordinator Service.

Other patched vulnerabilities include:

• CVE-2026-105477: Local privilege escalation in managed Veeam Agent for Linux installations, CVSS 7.3
• CVE-2026-108140: Arbitrary file writes through path traversal, CVSS 5.9
• CVE-2026-108141: Arbitrary file writes through path traversal, CVSS 5.9
• CVE-2026-107671: Veeam ONE administrator can bypass MFA by disabling it before completing verification, CVSS 8.5
⠀
Backup & Replication versions 13.0 and 13.1 are affected by the authorization and path-traversal flaws.

Older 12.x releases are not affected by those specific issues.
⠀
Administrators should update to:

• Backup & Replication 13.1.2 build 13.1.2.57
• Backup & Replication 13.0.3 build 13.0.3.63
• Veeam Agent for Linux 13.1.2 build 13.1.2.11
• Veeam ONE 13.1 P1 build 13.1.0.7940

posts.content:
Body-parser vulnerability CVE-2026-111181 (CVSS 7.5) enables Express denial of service with one request. Upgrade to body-parser 2.4.0 or 1.20.9.

#Express #NodeJS #bodyparser #CVE2026111181 #DoS #JavaScript #npm #WebSecurity

https://securityonline.info/body-parser-vulnerability-cve-2026-111181/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-111181.description:
### Impact

A single request can crash any application using `body-parser` with default options. When a request carries a `Content-Encoding` (for example `gzip`), `body-parser` pipes it into a decompression stream and, after reading the body, leaves that stream piped with no error listener. A payload of one valid compressed frame followed by trailing bytes decodes and the application responds normally, but the trailing bytes then reach the already-finished decoder, which emits an error that is re-thrown as an uncaught exception and terminates the process. No authentication or matching route is required, since parsing runs before routing.

### Patches

Fixed in body-parser 2.4.0 and 1.20.9. Upgrade to one of these versions.

### Workarounds

Pass `inflate: false` to the body-parser middleware if the application does not need to accept compressed request bodies. This rejects encoded requests before any decompression stream is created.

posts.content: kleor Contact Manager <=9.1.2 suffers CRITICAL (CVSS 9.8) file upload vuln (CVE-2026-109218). Unauthenticated users can exploit trailing dots to upload dangerous files, risking RCE. Harden configs & restrict uploads. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-109218-cwe-434-unrestricted-upload-of-file-with-dangerous-type-in-kleor-contact-manager-0a4841efd9c43b5a #OffSeq #WordPress #Infosec

CVE-2026-109218.description: The Contact Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 9.1.2 via the add_message function. This is due to an incomplete extension blacklist that fails to detect dangerous extensions when a trailing dot causes the extension-derivation routine to return an empty string, which sanitize_file_name() then silently removes before the file is written to disk. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Successful code execution additionally requires the server to use Apache with libapache2-mod-php (which maps .phar to PHP by default) and the attacker to retrieve the uploaded file within the brief window before it is removed by unlink() at end of request.

🚨🇺🇸 Microsoft Authenticator flaw allowed malicious Android apps to steal work account tokens

Tracked as CVE-2026-80097, the high-severity vulnerability allowed an Android app with no permissions to impersonate trusted Microsoft apps such as Teams and request tokens for a work account signed into Authenticator.
⠀
Researchers demonstrated that the stolen tokens could provide access to:

• Email and the ability to send messages
• Files stored in Microsoft services
• Calendars and Teams chats
• Authentication methods and passkey management
⠀
The flaw existed because Authenticator trusted identity information supplied by the requesting app instead of confirming which app actually made the request.
⠀
Microsoft rates the vulnerability 8.6 and says exploitation requires a malicious app on the device and user interaction during authentication. However, researchers reported obtaining tokens without further interaction when a work account was already signed in.
⠀
Microsoft says it has found no evidence of exploitation. The issue affects Authenticator for Android versions before 6.2606.4246.

Users should update to version 6.2606.4246 or later.

Source: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-80097

posts.content:
🔴 CVE-2026-110879 - Critical (9.8)

jackson-databind validates the outer class of a class-name type ID but accepts attacker-selected classes inside its generic arguments, even when those classes violate the declared type or would be rejected as direct type IDs. This bypasses the gen...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-110879/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-110879.description:
jackson-databind validates the outer class of a class-name type ID but accepts attacker-selected classes inside its generic arguments, even when those classes violate the declared type or would be rejected as direct type IDs. This bypasses the generic-argument validation added for CVE-2026-54512 (GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm), of which this is an incomplete fix.



DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() checks the outer class against the declared base type and then passes each argument from the type ID to _validateTypeParameter(), which validates the argument against the outer base type rather than enforcing its corresponding declared generic binding. It also invokes validators with arguments that have not passed the subtype check those validators expect. Under the default DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator this accepts an unrelated class inside a generic subtype even when the same class is rejected as a direct type ID. Where an allowIfBaseType(...) rule approves the outer type, Jackson substitutes LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator, so the configured validator no longer restricts the embedded arguments. The element type of a plain array type ID such as [Lpkg.Gadget; is likewise left unvalidated once the array's base type is approved.



Affected paths include annotation-based class-name polymorphism with a default Jackson 3.x JsonMapper, configured default typing in both Jackson 2.x and 3.x, and integrations that expose that default typing. The default-validator case requires no application-authored validator: with @JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS), a direct gadget type ID is rejected as "Not a subtype", while a type ID naming a generic wrapper around the same gadget is accepted and deserialized, including attacker-supplied bean properties. Where class-name default typing permits Map, a property declared as Map<String,String> accepts HashMap<FileSystemXmlApplicationContext,String>; map-key discovery then passes the attacker-controlled JSON property name to the selected class's one-string constructor. With Spring on the classpath and attacker-controlled XML the application can load, that constructor loads the XML and invokes ProcessBuilder.start() under the application account, giving arbitrary command execution.



This issue affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.10.0 and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0. Releases before 2.10.0 are not affected, because PolymorphicTypeValidator was introduced in jackson-databind 2.10.0.

posts.content:
🟠 CVE-2026-110747 - High (7.5)

ProtobufParser._readStringKey() reads the length prefix of a protobuf map entry's string key into an attacker-controlled int and then checks (_inputPtr + len) <= _inputEnd using signed arithmetic. For values near Integer.MAX_VALUE the addition ...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-110747/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-110747.description:
ProtobufParser._readStringKey() reads the length prefix of a protobuf map entry's string key into an attacker-controlled int and then checks (_inputPtr + len) <= _inputEnd using signed arithmetic. For values near Integer.MAX_VALUE the addition overflows to a negative value and the check passes even when the input contains no key data. The parser then calls _finishShortText(len), which expands the text buffer to the declared length via TextBuffer.expandCurrentSegment and Arrays.copyOf, throwing OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit.



An 8-byte malformed message containing a map entry with a declared key length of 0x7FFFFFFF is sufficient. Configured StreamReadConstraints, including maxStringLength, maxNameLength, maxDocumentLength and maxNestingDepth, do not prevent the failure. Applications running with -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError terminate the JVM.



This is the same integer-overflow pattern addressed for other call sites in the remediation associated with CVE-2026-104016 and CVE-2026-104017; the map-key call site was corrected on the 3.x branches only, leaving the corresponding 2.x branches unguarded. Release lines 2.18, 2.19 and 2.20 do not contain _readStringKey() and are not affected by this vector. No privileges or user interaction beyond the ability to submit data for parsing are required. The 3.0 release line and 3.1.0-3.1.5 / 3.2.0-3.2.1 do not contain _readStringKey() and are therefore not affected; the method first appears in 3.1.6 and 3.2.2, mirroring its introduction at 2.21.6 on the 2.x side.

CVE-2026-106013.description: The Jupiter X Core plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via the Twitter/X Social Login handler in all versions up to and including 4.61.0. The vulnerability exists within the verify_twitter_callback function because after exchanging the visitor's oauth_verifier for their access token, the handler never calls setOauthToken() to reassign the returned credentials to the TwitterOAuth client, causing the subsequent account/verify_credentials API call to remain signed with the site operator's stored Access Token and Access Token Secret rather than the authenticating visitor's token. posts.content:
PoC and full details are public for the Linux nf_tables vulnerability CVE-2026-23111. The kernelCTF exploit gains root and escapes containers. Patch now.

#Linux #LinuxKernel #nf_tables #Netfilter #CVE202623111 #kernelCTF #PoC #PrivilegeEscalation #ContainerEscape

https://securityonline.info/linux-nf-tables-vulnerability-cve-2026-23111-poc/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-23111.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_tables: fix inverted genmask check in nft_map_catchall_activate()

nft_map_catchall_activate() has an inverted element activity check
compared to its non-catchall counterpart nft_mapelem_activate() and
compared to what is logically required.

nft_map_catchall_activate() is called from the abort path to re-activate
catchall map elements that were deactivated during a failed transaction.
It should skip elements that are already active (they don't need
re-activation) and process elements that are inactive (they need to be
restored). Instead, the current code does the opposite: it skips inactive
elements and processes active ones.

Compare the non-catchall activate callback, which is correct:

  nft_mapelem_activate():
    if (nft_set_elem_active(ext, iter->genmask))
        return 0;   /* skip active, process inactive */

With the buggy catchall version:

  nft_map_catchall_activate():
    if (!nft_set_elem_active(ext, genmask))
        continue;   /* skip inactive, process active */

The consequence is that when a DELSET operation is aborted,
nft_setelem_data_activate() is never called for the catchall element.
For NFT_GOTO verdict elements, this means nft_data_hold() is never
called to restore the chain->use reference count. Each abort cycle
permanently decrements chain->use. Once chain->use reaches zero,
DELCHAIN succeeds and frees the chain while catchall verdict elements
still reference it, resulting in a use-after-free.

This is exploitable for local privilege escalation from an unprivileged
user via user namespaces + nftables on distributions that enable
CONFIG_USER_NS and CONFIG_NF_TABLES.

• Backup & Replication 13.0.3 build 13.0.3.63

### Impact
A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered in the CKEditor 5 engine. This vulnerability is caused by a prototype pollution issue in the `es-toolkit` library used in the CKEditor 5 codebase. This vulnerability could lead to unauthorized JavaScript code execution when the editor processes incoming `style` attribute values.

The underlying issue has been patched by the library maintainers, and the fix has been incorporated into CKEditor 5.

The problem has been recognized and patched. The fix will be available in version `48.5.1` (and above) and `47.7.4` (LTS).

Email us at [security@cksource.com](mailto:security@cksource.com) if you have any questions or comments about this advisory.

CVE-2026-57200.description: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. Prior to Asterisk 20.20.1, 21.12.3, 22.10.1, 23.4.1 and Certified Asterisk 22.8-cert3, an authenticated attacker with read-only permissions for the `Asterisk REST Interface (ARI)` may, under certain conditions, execute write operations through `REST-over-WebSocket`. The authorization bypass permits `arbitrary module path` loading and conditional remote code execution. The Asterisk HTTP web server must be enabled and reachable, and the attacker must already have valid `read-only ARI credentials`. HTTP is disabled by default and binds only to 127.0.0.1 by default even when enabled. This issue is fixed in Asterisk 20.20.1, 21.12.3, 22.10.1, 23.4.1 and Certified Asterisk 22.8-cert3.

Atlantis is a self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. From version 0.4.0 until 0.47.1, Atlantis passes the pull-request-controlled workspace value from atlantis.yaml into Terraform command argume...

CVE-2026-116676.description: Atlantis is a self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. From version 0.4.0 until 0.47.1, Atlantis passes the pull-request-controlled workspace value from atlantis.yaml into Terraform command arguments that are joined with strings.Join(args, " ") and executed through sh -c. An authenticated contributor whose pull request is eligible for an Atlantis plan can include shell metacharacters in the workspace name, causing arbitrary commands to execute as the Atlantis service account without custom workflows, apply permission, or a malicious Terraform provider. External contributors can reach the flaw through fork pull requests only when --allow-fork-prs is enabled, while eligible same-repository branches do not require that option. The commands inherit the Atlantis process environment and can access cloud-provider, Terraform, and version-control credentials as well as files, state, and network resources available to the service. This issue is fixed in version 0.47.1.

FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/indexing/indexingFiles.go resolves symbolic links through GetRealPath without confirming that the resolved ...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-116682/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-116682.description: FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/indexing/indexingFiles.go resolves symbolic links through GetRealPath without confirming that the resolved target remains inside the source root and the user's authorized scope. Download, preview, media, OnlyOffice, and public-share read flows that enable FollowSymlinks can therefore serve an out-of-scope target through a reachable in-scope symlink. An authenticated user with download access can read server-accessible files outside the assigned scope, and a holder of a public share link can do the same without an account when the shared directory exposes such a symlink. This issue is fixed in 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta.

posts.content:
Better than what?

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-114607

Better Auth is an authentication and authorization library for TypeScript. From 1.4.0-beta.18 until 1.7.7, deployments that enable Magic Link with storeToken set to plain, or with storeToken set to hashed and the global verification.storeIdentifier setting also set to hashed, enable a built-in social or Generic OAuth provider, and use account.storeStateStrategy set to database can accept an OAuth sign-in state value as a Magic Link token. These settings can cause Magic Link verification records and OAuth state to resolve to the same stored identifier, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to start OAuth sign-in for a known email address and redeem the returned state through Magic Link without controlling the mailbox or completing the provider callback. The attacker can obtain a normal session for an existing user, or create an account incorrectly marked as email verified when sign-up is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.7.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum

If a packet with bad checksum metadata gets into the ipv4 stack,
skb_checksum_help can corrupt the network header and cause a bunch of
mischief.

This was discovered and reported by Paulos, and has been reporoduced
by others independently since.

We really shouldn't allow such packets in, but as a defence
in depth measure, let's also check before we complete the checksum.

A more complete validation at input is forthcoming, but needs more work.

Apple Patches Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw and Hundreds of Vulnerabilities in October 2026 Security Update

On October 26, 2026, Apple released security updates across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS and Safari, patching several hundred vulnerabilities concentrated in WebKit, the kernel, ImageIO and CoreStorage. The fixes include WebKit code-execution and sandbox-escape flaws, a Remote Management remote code execution bug, and many privilege-escalation issues, plus the most urgent one: CVE-2026-86950 in CoreGraphics, which was exploited in targeted attacks and makes updating to iOS 18.7.11 critical for owners of older iPhones.

**If you use any Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV or Vision Pro), update it now. The current versions are iOS/iPadOS 27.2, 26.7.2 or 18.7.11, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, Tahoe 26.7.2 or Sequoia 15.8.2, tvOS/watchOS/visionOS 27.2, and Safari 27.2. If you still use an iPhone XS, XS Max or XR, install iOS 18.7.11 first: it fixes a flaw that has been exploited in targeted attacks. Until you've updated, be extra careful about unfamiliar websites, files, images and fonts from strangers, and connecting to unknown file-sharing or Screen Sharing servers.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #databreach
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/apple-addressed-329-unique-b-security-b-vulnerabilities-across-today-s-updates-9to5mac-y-u-w-g-y/gD2P6Ple2L

posts.content:
Wasmtime Patches Critical Sandbox Escape Flaws in Cranelift Compiler

Wasmtime fixed two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-115889 and CVE-2026-115893) that allow malicious WebAssembly modules to escape their sandboxes and execute arbitrary code on host systems. The flaws affect the Cranelift compiler and require immediate updates to Wasmtime 50.0.0 or other patched versions.

**If you use Wasmtime (directly, inside your own apps, or through tools like Spin), update ASAP to version 36.0.19, 48.0.7, 49.0.4 or 50.0.0, rebuild any applications that include it, and update Spin to 4.2.4. If you're still on the 24.x line, there is no patch, so upgrade to a supported version. If possible don't run WebAssembly code from sources you don't fully trust.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/wasmtime-patches-critical-sandbox-escape-flaws-in-cranelift-compiler-8-z-h-v-8/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-115889.description:
## Summary

In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox.

Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug.

## Impact

A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module.

## Patches

Wasmtime v36.0.19 has been released which fixes this issue.

Wasmtime fixed two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-115889 and CVE-2026-115893) that allow malicious WebAssembly modules to escape their sandboxes and execute arbitrary code on host systems. The flaws affect the Cranelift compiler and require immediate updates to Wasmtime 50.0.0 or other patched versions.

**If you use Wasmtime (directly, inside your own apps, or through tools like Spin), update ASAP to version 36.0.19, 48.0.7, 49.0.4 or 50.0.0, rebuild any applications that include it, and update Spin to 4.2.4. If you're still on the 24.x line, there is no patch, so upgrade to a supported version. If possible don't run WebAssembly code from sources you don't fully trust.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/wasmtime-patches-critical-sandbox-escape-flaws-in-cranelift-compiler-8-z-h-v-8/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-115893.description: Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br_table instruction with more than approximately 256,000 targets so that it has an incorrect conditional branch target. The branch can then jump to arbitrary other code at a user-controlled offset, allowing a user-controlled Wasm module to escape the sandbox on aarch64 engines using the default Cranelift backend. This issue is fixed in versions 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4.

posts.content: CVE-2026-92885: Qode Membership plugin (≤2.0.6.2) suffers a CRITICAL auth bypass (CVSS 9.8). Typo in Facebook OAuth check lets attackers hijack any WordPress account — including admins. Remove or restrict plugin use now. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-92885-cwe-287-improper-authentication-in-qode-themes-qode-membership-038e4dcfed22c95b #OffSeq #WordPress #Vuln

CVE-2026-92885.description: The Qode Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.6.2 via the qode_membership_check_facebook_user AJAX action. This is due to a typographic error in the Facebook OAuth token verification guard within the qode_membership_login_user_from_social_network function — the guard condition tests an undefined variable ($check_social_useqoder instead of $check_social_user), causing empty() to always return true and rendering the Graph API token verification branch dead code, leaving wp_set_auth_cookie() reachable with no credential or token validation whatsoever. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress account — including Administrator-level accounts — by supplying a known or enumerated administrator login name (rather than an email address) in the response[email] parameter, which the fallback path in get_user_by('login', $email) resolves to the matching account. Exploitation does require harvesting a valid qode_validate_facebook_login nonce, but this nonce is rendered on any public front-end page containing the [qode_user_login] or [qode_user_register] shortcode and is therefore obtainable without any prior authentication.

Rapid7 disclosed 17 Zimbra Collaboration Suite flaws, including CVE-2026-10632 and CVE-2026-93640, allowing XSS and root privilege escalation.

#Zimbra #Rapid7 #EmailSecurity #PrivilegeEscalation #XSS #Cybersecurity #Vulnerability #InfoSec

https://securityonline.info/zimbra-collaboration-suite-vulnerabilities-rapid7/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-93640.description: A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the optional dnscache package of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) allows the Unix zimbra account to access files with root privileges. The passwordless sudo policy permits arbitrary arguments to zmunbound, whose wrapper forwards them to Unbound without restricting the configuration path. An attacker can supply a configuration that retains root privileges and disables the chroot. Include directives expose root-readable file contents through parser errors, while an attacker-selected logfile path creates a root-owned file or appends Unbound log records to an existing file. This can disclose password hashes and private keys and corrupt privileged configuration files, preventing affected services from starting with the modified configuration. The affected configuration is present in ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.21 dnscache packages.

CVE-2026-10632.description: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Classic Web Client of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) allows an attacker to inject JavaScript through the packages parameter of the /h/rest document editor. The editor inserts package names into script attributes without HTML encoding. When combined with CVE-2026-50053, an attacker with an ordinary Zimbra account can supply their own authentication token and document identifiers in a URL and execute JavaScript in another signed-in user's Zimbra browser session when that user opens the URL. This permits reading mailbox data and performing authenticated actions as the victim. The issue affects ZCS 10.1.16 and was remediated in 10.1.17.
